'''Vincent Pilloni''' is a French mathematician, specializing in [[arithmetic geometry]] and the [[Langlands program]].

==Career==
Pilloni studied at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] and received his doctorate in 2009 from [[Université Sorbonne Paris Nord]] with thesis advisor [[Jacques Tilouine]] and thesis ''Arithmétique des variétés de Siegel''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=144732}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis|title=''Arithmétique des variétés de Siegel'' par Vincent Pilloni|website=theses.fr|date=January 2009|url=http://www.theses.fr/2009PA132011|type=These de doctorat|last1=Pilloni|first1=Vincent}}</ref>

His research deals with, among other topics, the question of how the [[modularity theorem]] for [[elliptic curve]]s over the rational numbers (which led to the proof of [[Fermat's Last Theorem]]) can be extended to [[Abelian variety|abelian varieties]]. With George Boxer, [[Frank Calegari]] and [[Toby Gee]], he proved that all abelian surfaces and genus two curves over totally real fields are potentially modular and satisfy the [[Hasse-Weil conjecture]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Boxer |first1=George |last2=Calegari |first2=Frank |last3=Gee |first3=Toby |last4=Pilloni |first4=Vincent |date=2021-12-01 |title=Abelian surfaces over totally real fields are potentially modular |journal=Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS |language=en |volume=134 |issue=1 |pages=153–501 |doi=10.1007/s10240-021-00128-2 |issn=1618-1913|doi-access=free |arxiv=1812.09269 }}</ref>

Pilloni is a ''[[:fr:Directeur_de_recherche_au_CNRS|Chargé de recherche]]'' of [[CNRS]] at [[Paris-Saclay University]] based at the [[:fr:Institut_de_mathématique_d'Orsay|Institut de mathématique d'Orsay]].

In 2018 he was an invited speaker, with Fabrizio Andreatta and Adrian Iovita, at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.<ref>{{cite book|author=Andreatta, Fabrizio|author2=Iovita, Adrian|author3=Pilloni, Vincent|chapter=p-adic variation of automorphic sheaves|title=Proc. Int. Long. of Math. – 2018 Rio de Janeiro|volume=1|pages=291–318|chapter-url=http://perso.ens-lyon.fr/vincent.pilloni/ICM.pdf}}</ref> In 2018 Pilloni received the [[Prix Élie Cartan]]. In 2021 he was awarded the [[Fermat Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/spip.php?article1073&lang=fr|title=Institut de Mathématiques de Toulouse – Fermat Prize 2021|website=www.math.univ-toulouse.fr|accessdate=17 December 2021|archive-date=14 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211214233029/https://www.math.univ-toulouse.fr/spip.php?article1073&lang=fr|url-status=dead}}</ref>
